19-013.r: Ministries are allotted to Ministers by the President on the PM's advice; Ministries are NOT created by the PM on the Cabinet Secretary's advice.
19-013.t: Cabinet Secretary heads the Cabinet Secretariat and chairs the Civil Services Board; he does not create Ministries.

19-014.r: Art 77(3) → President makes rules of business and allocates portfolios among ministers on the PM's advice; PM and Cabinet Secretary do not 'form' Ministries.

19-015.r: Parliamentary form of government → actual/real executive power exercised by the Prime Minister (Article 75).

19-016.r: Art 77(1) → all executive action taken in the name of the President (not PM); Art 77(3) → President makes rules for business and its allocation among Ministers.
19-016.t: Don't pick 'in the name of the Prime Minister'; executive action is always in the President's name.

19-017.r: PM from Rajya Sabha can speak in Lok Sabha but cannot vote there → cannot vote in his own favour in a no-confidence motion.
19-017.h: Speak in both Houses, vote only in your own House.

19-018.r: Article 75 → appointment of PM and Ministers (75(1)); Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President (75(2)).
hi: Pleasure of the President (राष्ट्रपति का प्रसाद)

19-019.r: PM is generally a Lok Sabha member, but not compulsorily; can be from Rajya Sabha; Indira Gandhi → first PM from Rajya Sabha at appointment.

19-020.r: Art 75(5) → PM need not be an MP at appointment, but must become a member of either House (LS or RS) within 6 months.
19-020.t: Don't pick 'must join Lok Sabha'; any one House of Parliament is enough.

19-021.r: Minimum age to become Prime Minister → 25 years (same as for a Lok Sabha member).

19-022.r: Art 75(1) → PM appointed by the President; other Ministers appointed by President on PM's advice; not elected by Lok Sabha or Parliament.

19-023.r: PM has full discretion in choosing ministers (Art 75(1)); a non-member minister must enter either House within 6 consecutive months, else ceases (Art 75(5)).

19-027.r: Cabinet membership is NOT restricted to the Lower House; a non-member can be minister for 6 months (Art 75(5)); cabinet needs Lok Sabha majority confidence.

19-028.r: Prime Minister (with Council of Ministers) → collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Art 75(3)), not to the President or Cabinet.

19-029.r: Collective responsibility → to the House of the People; a constitutional obligation under Article 75(3); Article 74(3) does not exist.

19-030.r: Council of Ministers → collectively responsible to Lok Sabha; when Lok Sabha is not an option, the nearest answer is Parliament.

19-033.r: Union Council of Ministers → collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha (Art 75(3)).
19-033.t: Don't pick 'Parliament' when 'Only to Lok Sabha' is offered; Rajya Sabha cannot remove the ministry.

19-035.r: (A) false: Council responsible only to Lok Sabha (Art 75(3)); (R) true: members of either House can be Union Ministers, but vote only in own House.

19-036.r: Council responsible to Lok Sabha, not 'Parliament' (Art 75(3)); Ministers hold office at President's pleasure (75(2)); PM communicates legislative proposals to President (Art 78(a)).

19-037.r: PM resigning on losing majority in Lok Sabha → a convention, not written in the Constitution (flows from collective responsibility, Art 75(3)).

19-038.r: In Indian polity, the Executive is subordinate to the Legislature; Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the House of the People.

19-039.r: Council of Ministers can move a Confidence Motion; No-Confidence Motion only in Lok Sabha; if passed by Lok Sabha majority → Council must resign.
19-039.t: Don't confuse Confidence Motion (moved by the government) with No-Confidence/Censure Motion (moved against it).

19-041.r: A minister who resigns may make a statement on his resignation in Lok Sabha with the Speaker's permission; he cannot be compelled to do so.

19-042.r: No-Confidence Motion against the Council of Ministers in Lok Sabha → needs at least 50 members to table it.

19-044.r: No-Confidence Motion: not mentioned in the Constitution; introduced only in Lok Sabha; procedure in Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure (Rule 198).

19-045.r: No-Confidence Motion: only in Lok Sabha (Rule 198); notice to Secretary-General, not Speaker; 28 such motions and 11 confidence motions till 15 August 2023; first by J.B. Kripalani (1963).
19-045.c: Per the explanation, (a) is wrong (28 no-confidence and 11 confidence motions) and so is (c) (notice goes to the Secretary-General, not the Speaker); the Commission deleted the question.

19-046.r: Resignation of Council of Ministers does NOT bring President's Rule; President asks it to continue till an alternative arrangement (new government or early election).

19-047.r: Kailash Nath Katju (Madhya Pradesh) → in Nehru's Cabinet: Law Minister and Home Minister 1951, Defence Minister 1955; CM of Madhya Pradesh 1957-1962.
19-047.c: Question says Defence first, then Home; the explanation gives Home (1951) before Defence (1955).

19-048.r: First Finance Minister of independent India → R.K. Shanmukham Chetty (1947-1948), in Nehru's Cabinet.

19-049.r: First Law Minister of independent India → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar; Law Minister in the 1946 Interim Government → Jogendra Nath Mandal.
19-049.t: Don't confuse the first Cabinet (Ambedkar) with the Interim Government of 1946 (Jogendra Nath Mandal).

19-050.r: C.H. Bhabha → Works, Mines and Power (Interim Govt 1946) → Commerce (first Cabinet 1947); Rajendra Prasad, Jagjivan Ram, Baldev Singh kept same portfolios.

19-051.r: 12th Prime Minister of India → H.D. Deve Gowda (counting acting PM Gulzari Lal Nanda); Narendra Modi → 15th PM.

19-052.r: PM tenures: V.P. Singh 1989-90; Chandra Shekhar 1990-91; Deve Gowda 1996-97; I.K. Gujral 1997-98; Atal Bihari Vajpayee 1999-2004.
19-052.h: Order VP → Chandra Shekhar → Deve Gowda → Gujral → Vajpayee follows the years 1989 to 1999.

19-053.r: PM more than once → Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi, Gulzari Lal Nanda (acting PM twice), Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

19-054.r: PM more than once with gaps → Gulzari Lal Nanda (1964, 1966), Indira Gandhi (1966-1977, 1980-1984), Vajpayee (1996, 1998-2004); not Nehru or Shastri.

19-055.r: PM who died outside India → Lal Bahadur Shastri (second PM), in Tashkent (capital of Uzbekistan), 11 January 1966.

19-056.r: CMs who became PM: Narasimha Rao → undivided Andhra Pradesh; Morarji Desai → Bombay; Deve Gowda → Karnataka; Charan Singh → undivided Uttar Pradesh; Modi → Gujarat.

19-057.r: Never a Chief Minister before becoming PM → Chandra Shekhar; Deve Gowda, Narasimha Rao and Morarji Desai were CMs earlier.

19-058.r: Not a CM of any state before becoming PM → Chandra Shekhar; Morarji Desai, P.V. Narasimha Rao and Charan Singh had been CMs.

19-059.r: Lok Sabha member while PM → Chandra Shekhar (PM 1990-1991, MP from Balia); Deve Gowda, I.K. Gujral, Manmohan Singh were not LS members then.

19-060.r: PM who never attended Parliament → Chaudhari Charan Singh (28 July 1979 - 14 January 1980); Congress withdrew support before Lok Sabha sat.

19-061.r: All were Union Finance Ministers: V.P. Singh (1984-87), R. Venkataraman (1980-82), Y.B. Chavan (1971-75), Pranab Mukherjee (2009-2012).

19-062.r: LPG (Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) New Economic Policy → announced by PM P.V. Narasimha Rao, 24 July 1991.

19-063.r: Dr. Manmohan Singh → former Finance Minister, RBI Governor and India's representative at IMF; never Chairman of the Finance Commission.

19-064.r: Manmohan Singh (PM 2004-2014) → Rajya Sabha member from Assam (1991, 1996, 2001, 2007, 2013); from Rajasthan in 2019.

19-065.r: Both true, R not the explanation: ministers make policy and civil servants follow it; parliamentary government works on cabinet collective responsibility.

19-066.r: Deputy PM: not in the Constitution; a conventional title given to a Cabinet Minister (political decision); confers no PM powers. A and R true, R not explanation.

19-067.r: Office of Deputy Prime Minister → extra-constitutional growth; not mentioned in the Constitution, created by political necessity.
19-067.t: Not created by the 44th or 85th Amendment; no amendment created it.

19-068.r: First Deputy PM → Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (15 August 1947 - 15 December 1950), also Home Minister; integrated over 500 princely states.

19-069.r: Union executive power → vested in President (Art 53(1)), not PM; ex-officio Chairman of Civil Services Board → Cabinet Secretary, not PM.
19-069.t: PM has direct charge of the Cabinet Secretariat, but the Cabinet Secretary chairs the Civil Services Board.

19-070.r: No rule that Cabinet Ministers must be Lok Sabha members; Cabinet Secretariat works under the PM's Office, not the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.

19-071.r: Cabinet Committees: extra-constitutional (Rules of Business), set up by PM; if PM is a member he must chair; Parliamentary Affairs Committee chaired by Defence Minister.

19-072.r: 91st Amendment Act, 2003 → Council of Ministers incl. PM max 15% of Lok Sabha strength; added as Article 75(1A).
